0.value:
crossfade_scanner turns one number from 0 to 1 into a walk through a chain of sounds, as a fade list for a polyphonic sampler.

Any single continuous control - a limb height, a distance, a fader - becomes a path through a set of sounds.

HOW THE RANGE IS DIVIDED:
0 to 1 is split into 'n' equal sections, one per sound. At 0 everything is silent. Through the first section the first sound fades up to full. Through each section after that the previous sound fades out as the next fades in. At 1 the last sound is at full and the rest are silent. So with 4 sounds, 0.25 is the first alone, 0.375 is the first and second at half each, and 0.5 is the second alone.

'equal_power' bends each level along a quarter sine, so that at the middle of a crossover both sounds sit at about 0.71 rather than 0.5 - the loudness holds steady through the crossover instead of dipping.

WHICH SOUNDS:
By default the sound ids are 0 to n-1. Send a list of ids to 'sound_ids' to choose them - its length becomes n. Changing 'n' afterwards goes back to 0 to n-1. The ids are saved with the patch.

WHAT IT SENDS:
The whole list - every sound with its level, silent ones at 0 - each time the value, n, the ids or equal_power changes.

THE fade LIST:
[[sound_id, level], ...] is what a polyphonic sampler's 'fade' inlet takes:
each listed sound plays at its level, and a sound at 0 is silenced. So the whole crossfade is one message.

SYNTAX:
crossfade_scanner

It takes no arguments.

EXAMPLE:
crossfade_scanner

INPUTS and PARAMETERS:

value:
The position along the chain, 0 to 1.

n:
How many sounds, 2 to 128. 4 by default.

sound_ids:
A list of sound ids; sets n to its length.

equal_power:
Hold the loudness through each crossover.

OUTPUTS:

fade:
The [sound_id, level] list.

RELATED:
polyphonic_sampler~ plays the list. effort_fader and muscle_activation_fader make fade lists from body data. crossfade blends two values.
